Hint level selector

Today, Hint shows one line and each further click shows the next (A). The new Hint opens a choice first: Notice, Interpret and Act, where each is unlocked only after the one before it has been read, and Find when the scene points at a destination. B puts that choice in the scribe's strip, so the scroll stays in view and play carries on. C puts it in a box over the scene like the Journal, which pauses the game and has more room. Both open on the choices without showing any text. All text is from the levels' puzzles.json files; the pictures are screenshots of the game at 1280 × 720.

A · Today: one Hint button, repeated clicks

Every click on Hint shows the next authored line in the strip, and the line asks you to click again. Nothing to choose, nothing to read again.

B · Bottom band: the strip becomes the selector

Hint opens a row of choices in the scribe's strip, with the chosen hint under it. The strip keeps its height, the scroll stays in view, and the game carries on while you read.

C · Modal: a box over the scene, the game pauses

Hint opens a papyrus box in the Journal's style. It has room for the longest hint and a timed game stops while you read, but the box covers part of what you are looking at.

What to look at
CaseOffering table has all three levels and a Notice that points at something on screen. Standard-bearers has two. Find is one option. Apep is the longest authored hint (146 characters) in a timed fight. Crocodiles has two levels in a timed fight (the picture is the Apep fight's).
Both sizes1280 × 720 is the game's frame. 640 × 480 is the smallest window the UI tests cover; its scene is scaled to fit and is not 1:1. Look at the FITS / OVERFLOWS line under each frame.
Open questionsPressing the Hint icon while the selector is open: close it, or do nothing? Shown here: it closes. Should Esc and a click beside the modal both close it? Shown here: both do, as with the Journal.
